Article 19
(1) The implementation of Protection for female domestic workers is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel treatment, inhumane treatment, degradation of human dignity, and exploitation in employment relationships.
(2) Female domestic workers as referred to in paragraph (1) receive protection for:
a. recognition of rights, wages, and decent working conditions;
b. health insurance and social security;
c. access to information and legal consultation services; and
d. opportunities to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

Article 11
(1) Women have the right to obtain health services in order to undergo a reproductive life and sexual life that is healthy, safe, and free from coercion and/or violence.
(2) Health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. health services for the period before pregnancy, childbirth and after giving birth;
b. pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services and sexual health; and
c. reproductive health services.
d. health services that are implemented through promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative approaches.

Tenth Part
Women Victims of Violence

Part One
Prevention of Violence Against Women

Third Part
Rights of Women Victims of Violence

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency Area is Pangandaran Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Pangandaran.
3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as Women.
6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women. 7. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities. 8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily. 9. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred.
10. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
11. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim.
12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals.
13. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 3 certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death.
15. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Household Neglect is a person who neglects a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
18. Human Trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.
jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 4
20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Household Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household environment.
21. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of the Woman.
22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women.
24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions.
25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
26. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and Women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings so they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
27. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and Women.
28. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can carry out their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
29. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions normally.
30. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their area of origin.
jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 5
31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
32. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and children victims of violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance.
33. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports, complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and Social Reintegration for Women Victims of Violence.

Article 42
(1) Regional Government conducts evaluation on the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women at the end of each fiscal year.
(2) The results of the evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women in the following year.
(3) The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 31
The obligations of family and parents as referred to in Article 25 letter c and letter d are in the form of full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women as family members.

ELUCIDATION

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PANGANDARAN REGENCY
NUMBER YEAR 2019
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Fundamentally, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize community welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining national unity, integrity and harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all fields of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems especially towards women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physical, psychological, sexual and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by regional governments. The high number of cases of violence against women are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

Regional Governments are obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishment of P2TP2A, guaranteeing the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 36
(1) The provision of services for the Protection of Women as referred to in Article 35 consists of identification of Victims, legal aid, medical rehabilitation, psychosocial rehabilitation, Social Reintegration, repatriation assistance, or other forms.
(2) The provision of services for the Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided for Women Victims of Violence including Victims of Human Trafficking, Women in disaster-prone areas, Women workers, elderly Women, Women with disabilities, Women Victims of sexual exploitation, Women heads of households, and Women from other vulnerable groups.

Article 40
(1) The Regional Government shall establish a forum for the protection of women victims of violence at every sub-district level.
(2) The forum for the protection of women victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall have the duties to:
a. coordinate and synchronize the handling of protection services for women victims of violence;
b. facilitate and provide more optimal services and reach out to lower level communities;
c. maintain and develop networks and referral systems; and
d. compile a database regarding the development of protection for women victims of violence.

Article 30
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 25 letter b shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
(2) The forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan and/or village level;
b. establishing women's protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's rights; d. providing first aid to victims; and e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment; (3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.
(4) Provisions regarding the forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PANGANDARAN REGENCY
NUMBER YEAR 2019
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Fundamentally, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize community welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining national unity, integrity and harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all fields of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems especially towards women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physical, psychological, sexual and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by regional governments. The high number of cases of violence against women are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

Regional Governments are obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishment of P2TP2A, guaranteeing the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PANGANDARAN REGENCY
NUMBER YEAR 2019
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Fundamentally, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize community welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining national unity, integrity and harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all fields of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems especially towards women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physical, psychological, sexual and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by regional governments. The high number of cases of violence against women are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

Regional Governments are obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishment of P2TP2A, guaranteeing the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PANGANDARAN REGENCY
NUMBER YEAR 2019
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Fundamentally, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize community welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining national unity, integrity and harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all fields of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems especially towards women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physical, psychological, sexual and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by regional governments. The high number of cases of violence against women are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

Regional Governments are obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishment of P2TP2A, guaranteeing the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PANGANDARAN REGENCY
NUMBER YEAR 2019
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Fundamentally, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize community welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining national unity, integrity and harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all fields of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems especially towards women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physical, psychological, sexual and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by regional governments. The high number of cases of violence against women are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

Regional Governments are obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishment of P2TP2A, guaranteeing the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PANGANDARAN REGENCY
NUMBER YEAR 2019
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Fundamentally, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize community welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining national unity, integrity and harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all fields of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems especially towards women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physical, psychological, sexual and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by regional governments. The high number of cases of violence against women are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

Regional Governments are obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishment of P2TP2A, guaranteeing the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency Area is Pangandaran Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Pangandaran.
3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as Women.
6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women. 7. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities. 8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily. 9. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred.
10. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
11. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim.
12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals.
13. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 3 certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death.
15. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Household Neglect is a person who neglects a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
18. Human Trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Household Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household environment.
21. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of the Woman.
22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women.
24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions.
25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
26. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and Women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings so they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
27. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and Women.
28. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can carry out their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
29. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions normally.
30. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their area of origin.

31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
32. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and children victims of violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance.
33. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports, complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and Social Reintegration for Women Victims of Violence.

NUMBER YEAR 2019
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Fundamentally, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize community welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining national unity, integrity and harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all fields of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems especially towards women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physical, psychological, sexual and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by regional governments. The high number of cases of violence against women are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

Regional Governments are obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishment of P2TP2A, guaranteeing the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

CHAPTER VI
STRATEGY FOR WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION
Article 32
(1) Women's empowerment and protection shall be implemented by integrating gender mainstreaming and gender-disaggregated data in an integrated manner based on laws and regulations.
(2) In women's empowerment and protection, a Working Group and Integrated Services shall be established as determined by Regent's Decree.
(3) Women's empowerment and protection shall be coordinated by the Agency handling Women's Empowerment.

Article 42
(1) Regional Government conducts evaluation on the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women at the end of each fiscal year.
(2) The results of the evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women in the following year.
(3) The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

19. ELUCIDATION

NUMBER YEAR 2019
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Fundamentally, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize community welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining national unity, integrity and harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all fields of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems especially towards women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physical, psychological, sexual and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by regional governments. The high number of cases of violence against women are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

Regional Governments are obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishment of P2TP2A, guaranteeing the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

NUMBER YEAR 2019
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Fundamentally, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize community welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining national unity, integrity and harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all fields of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems especially towards women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physical, psychological, sexual and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by regional governments. The high number of cases of violence against women are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

Regional Governments are obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishment of P2TP2A, guaranteeing the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
